newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares staged a late rally on Thursday as futures related buying helped shed their earlier losses to finish firmer.
Gold shares sank to fresh four-year lows as woes on the weak bullion price pervaded the market.
Industrials initially perked up in the wake of the Dow Jones index's 180-point rise overnight, but retreated at noon as the morning euphoria gave way to pessimism over local factors.
Dealers cited lingering concerns about high local interest rates and the possibility that they might rise as one of the main dampners on sentiment.

"There is a depressing mindset creeping into the market. If Wall Street jumps the local market does not jump. When the U.S. cut interest rates ours rise. And when theirs rise ours do not come down," a dealer said.
But futures-related demand inspired by early gains on the S&P index helped the market firmer at the finish.
On Wall Street, stocks opened lower after a strong U.S. gross domestic product figure rekindled inflationery fears.
Dealers said the local market was generally quiet in the afternoon session ahead of the Workers Day market holiday on Thursday.
On the gold board, shares lurched lower as an uninspiring bullion priced continued to lurk around the $340 an ounce level.
"We need the gold price to run before there will be any interest in the sector," one trader said.
Volumes in general were average after Tuesday's record breaking turnover.
The overall index ended up 23.5 points at 7,130.5, the industrial index gained 41.5 points to 8,494.3 points and the gold index dropped 18.2 points to fresh four-year low of 1,187.0 points.
The financial index ended at a record high for the second consecutive day. It added 54.2 points to 8,960.0 points.
Features on Wednesday included personnel services firm, Technihire, which dropped nearly nine percent, or seven cents, to 71 cents after a profit warning issued earlier.
Technihire warned that it had significant debtors who may not be in a position to repay monies due to the firm in full or within a reasonable period of time which could lead to losses in the company.
Tourvest was up four cents to 152 cents and Foodcorp rose 60 cents to a year high of 32.50 rand with both shares' volumes boosted by bookovers.
Near-dated share futures ended a rollercoaster day firmer after reacting to a strong Wall Street overnight which leapt over 179 points -- its second biggest one-day point gain.
Dealers said the market was quiet volatile with trade following movements in the U.S. S&P futures but volumes were thin. Gold contracts ended weak on the lacklustre bullion price.
The market was seen looking to Wall Street on Friday for further direction but underlying sentiment was still firm, dealers said.
The June all-share contract stood at 6,620/35 from 6,606, the industrial contract is at 8,322/29 from 8,310 and the gold contract is at 833/40 from 841.
-- Charles Phahlane, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
